title: Complex-Valued Probability Measures and Their Applications in Information Theory
summary: This paper introduces a comprehensive framework for complex-valued probability measures and explores their novel applications in information theory and statistical analysis. We define a complex probability measure as a phase-modulated extension of a classical probability measure. Building upon this foundation, we propose three fundamental information-theoretic quantities: complex entropy, which quantifies distribution uniformity through phase coherence; complex divergence, an asymmetric measure of dissimilarity between distributions; and the complex metric, a symmetric distance function…
